name: Enviro Infra Engineers
tagline: Water/wastewater EPC+HAM with a surging order book, but cash conversion, ROCE trend and margin are the real test
verdict_headline: Strong government-backed order-book growth undercut by a sharp ROCE decline, working-capital stress and negative operating cash flow
verdict_reasoning: Four-box score 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation weak) permits 10x-in-2-3-years, but conviction set separately
Order book surged 242% YoY to Rs6,813.6cr (~6.4x FY26 revenue), split water/wastewater (~Rs3,694cr) and a new renewables/BESS leg (~Rs3,027cr) after entry via the Suyog Urja platform

But ROCE has declined every year since listing (59% FY22 -> 47% -> 32% -> ~20% FY25/26) and Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 18.70% from 25.31% YoY, prompting an exchange Reg.33 clarification request (response pending)

Working-capital cycle stretched from 24 days (FY24) to 137-166 days (FY26) on unbilled revenue tied to delayed AMRUT fund releases; operating cash flow has been negative for two straight years despite reported profits
Borrowings rose 80% (Rs234cr FY24 -> Rs422cr FY26) and no dividend has been paid despite consistent profitability -- real earnings-quality downgrade from the light-pass view
business_overview: Enviro Infra Engineers (EIEL), promoted by the Jain family (founded 1991 by late Rajinder Kumar Jain; listed Dec 2024) is a Delhi-based water and wastewater infrastructure EPC and Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) contractor executing projects under Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT and Namami Gange. FY26 marked its diversification into renewable energy/BESS EPC via the Suyog Urja acquisition, now ~44% of the order book.
fundamentals_table: ~20% FY25/26, declining from 59% FY22, 47% FY23, 32% FY24
None paid in any year despite consistent profits
fundamentals_narrative: Top-line momentum is real: revenue grew from Rs224cr (FY22) to Rs1,146cr (FY26), a 56% CAGR, with Q1 FY27 reaccelerating to +49% YoY on a surging order book (+242% YoY to Rs6,814cr, ~6.4x FY26 revenue, 24-36mo visibility) spanning water/wastewater EPC+HAM and a new renewables/BESS leg. But capital efficiency has deteriorated sharply as the balance sheet has grown post-IPO: ROCE fell from 59% (FY22) to ~20% (FY25/26), and Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin cratered to 18.70% from 25.31% YoY on higher execution costs and lower-margin IPP work, triggering an exchange query on the results (response pending). The working-capital cycle stretched from 24 days (FY24) to 137-166 days (FY26) as unbilled revenue (195 days) built up against delayed AMRUT state fund releases, pushing operating cash flow negative for two straight years (-Rs59cr FY25, -Rs63cr FY26) despite consistently reported profits, and borrowings rose 80% to Rs422cr to bridge the gap. Management guides FY27 revenue of Rs2,000cr at a 19-20% blended EBITDA margin (water 21-22%, renewables/BESS 15-18%) and working-capital normalization toward ~90 days once fund releases resume -- both unconfirmed. No dividend has ever been paid despite the profit track record.
bse_notes: Mar 2026: five projects worth Rs1,481cr won, including the company's first BESS orders (4 NTPC projects, Rs1,070cr). Jul 2026: two HAM projects from UP Jal Nigam (Rural) under Namami Gange, combined Rs256.92cr, taking the HAM portfolio to five projects. Sep 2026: Rs189.99cr confirmed order from Tata Power Renewable Energy awarded to step-down subsidiary Suyog Urja Limited (Sep 7, 2026). Exchange sought Reg.33 clarification on Q4 FY26 results; company response pending as of this review.
bull_case: Order book surged 242% YoY to Rs6,814cr (~6.4x FY26 revenue), 24-36mo visibility, diversified across JJM/AMRUT/Namami Gange water-sewage EPC+HAM plus new renewables/BESS wins (NTPC Rs1,070cr, Tata Power Rs190cr)

JJM 2.0 extended to 2028 plus AMRUT/Namami Gange give a structural multi-year government water-infra tailwind; India's BESS/renewables buildout adds a second large growth avenue via the Suyog Urja platform (1,200MW execution experience, ~1,702MW active pipeline)
Revenue growth reaccelerated sharply in Q1 FY27 (+49% YoY) after a soft FY26, with five HAM projects now in the portfolio providing longer-duration, annuity-like revenue

At ~17.6x trailing P/E the stock is not expensive for a company that has compounded revenue at a 56% 5yr CAGR, if margin and cash conversion stabilize per FY27 guidance (19-20% blended EBITDA margin, WC normalizing toward ~90 days)
bear_case: ROCE has fallen sharply and consistently: 59% (FY22) -> 47% (FY23) -> 32% (FY24) -> ~20% (FY25/26), while Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin cratered to 18.70% from 25.31% YoY -- capital efficiency is deteriorating even as the balance sheet grows

Working-capital cycle ballooned from 24 days (FY24) to 137-166 days (FY26) on unbilled revenue (195 days) tied to delayed AMRUT fund releases; operating cash flow has been negative for two straight years (-Rs59cr FY25, -Rs63cr FY26) despite reported profits

Borrowings grew 80% (Rs234cr FY24 -> Rs422cr FY26) to fund the cash gap, no dividend has been paid despite consistent profitability, and the exchange sought a Reg.33 clarification on the Q4 FY26 results (response pending as of this review)

No real pricing power: wins are competitive-bid EPC/HAM, moat is weak, and the renewables/BESS diversification targets a lower 10-12% PAT margin than the core water business, diluting blended profitability as the mix shifts
FII+DII combined holding fell from ~6.6% to ~1.4% over roughly six quarters even as promoter holding stayed flat -- institutional investors have been net sellers through the growth story

Renewables/BESS is now ~Rs3,027cr (44%) of the order book after a standing start in FY26 -- a genuine second growth leg, but targeted at a structurally lower 10-12% PAT margin than the water business

open_questions: What specifically did the exchange query on Q4 FY26 results, and how did the company respond?
Will the Rs6,800cr+ order book's cash conversion actually normalize to ~90 WC days once AMRUT fund releases resume, or is this structural to government-funded EPC?
Can renewables/BESS scale profitably at the targeted 10-12% PAT margin, or will the lower-margin mix structurally cap blended profitability as the segment's order-book share grows?
FY24 operating-cash-flow figure was not independently sourced this pass -- would help confirm whether the negative-OCF pattern started in FY25 or earlier
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Low-Medium. Order-book strength (Rs6,814cr, +242% YoY) and a genuine structural water-infra + new BESS tailwind are real, but the deep dive surfaced a sharply declining ROCE (59%->~20% since FY22), two years of negative operating cash flow, an 80% jump in borrowings, a stretched 137-166 day working-capital cycle, zero dividends despite consistent profits, and a pending exchange query on Q4 FY26 results -- collectively a meaningful earnings-quality downgrade from the light-pass view.

FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs2,000cr
commitments.dependency: order execution pace + government fund releases

commitments.single_point_of_failure: government fund-release cycle, outside company's control

earnings_chain.bottleneck_link: government fund-release timing (drives both revenue recognition and cash conversion)
earnings_chain.operating_leverage: unclear -- revenue growing fast via order execution but EBITDA margin has compressed (Q4 FY26 18.70% vs 25.31% YoY), so scale has not yet translated into margin expansion
evidenced_links: order book execution (orders won, contracts signed)
assumed_links: margin normalization to the 19-22% guided range

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~15-18% EPS CAGR FY26-28 to justify 17.6x against a ~20-22x re-rated exit for a mid-teens-growth infra EPC compounder
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: Revenue toward management's Rs2,000cr guide (+~75% YoY) but EBITDA margin likely nearer the guided 19-20% blended vs FY26's 24.2%, so PAT growth more modest than revenue growth, roughly +15-25%
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: Second leg from renewables/BESS order book scaling (Rs3,000cr+ orders in hand) plus water segment normalizing; PAT growth dependent on working-capital/cash-conversion actually improving, not just revenue
market_expectation.gap_basis: Market has already re-rated the order-book growth story (17.6x P/E, up from ~12x at the light-pass stage); base-case reverse-P/E math lands close to CMP, so margin-compression and working-capital/cash-conversion risk look roughly reflected rather than ignored -- upside needs the guided margin/WC normalization to actually hold
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: Q2/Q3 FY27 results showing EBITDA margin trajectory toward the guided 19-22% and working-capital days normalizing toward ~90

value_chain.theme: government-funded water/wastewater infrastructure (JJM/AMRUT/Namami Gange) EPC+HAM, diversifying into renewable energy/BESS EPC
value_chain.position: EPC + HAM contractor/developer -- designs, builds and (under HAM) operates treatment plants; now also a BESS/solar/wind EPC player via Suyog Urja
value_chain.bottleneck_node: government fund-release cycle + competitive-bid execution capacity
value_chain.note: Multiple players are chasing an expanding but still government-funding-dependent order pipeline; limited pricing power because wins are tender-based, not negotiated -- capital-cycle read is 'adding', a late-cycle risk if fund-release delays persist across the sector.

drivers: Shift in revenue mix toward lower-margin renewables/BESS (10-12% PAT margin target vs the water business)
Government fund-release delays causing unbilled-revenue buildup that distorts quarterly margin recognition
Q4 FY26 one-off cost pressure: design-stage delays + input-cost spikes
earnings_quality.normalised_note: FY25's 25% EBITDA margin likely reflects favorable mix/timing; FY27's guided blended margin of 19-20% (water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%) is probably closer to a sustainable through-cycle level.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Revenue YoY: FY23 +51%, FY24 +116%, FY25 +46%, FY26 +7.5%, Q1 FY27 +49% -- order/project-driven and highly uneven; PAT growth lagged revenue growth sharply in FY26/Q1 FY27 (+6.4%, +6.5%) despite strong topline, signalling margin compression rather than demand slowdown.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At ~17.6x trailing P/E (EPS ~Rs10.7 on Rs188cr PAT), roughly an 18-20% EPS CAGR FY26-28 is needed to justify a steady re-rating toward a 22-25x compounder multiple; FY27 guidance (revenue Rs2,000cr, blended margin 19-20%) implies PAT growth more modest than that if margin stays compressed -- a close call, not clearly priced-in or clearly cheap.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Reinvesting IPO proceeds + new borrowings into working capital and the Suyog Urja renewables/BESS acquisition; incremental ROCE has fallen sharply (59%->~20%) as the capital base grew, though some of that reflects a low initial base rather than poor project-level returns
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit diversification from core water/wastewater EPC into renewable energy/BESS EPC via the Suyog Urja platform (1,200MW execution experience, ~1,702MW pipeline)

track_record.note: FY23-FY25 cleared both tests (revenue growth >=10%, ROCE >=15%); FY26 revenue growth slowed to 7.5% (just below the 10% bar) even as ROCE held ~20% -- order-book-driven lumpiness, not a structural break. FY22 excluded for lack of a prior-year base to measure growth against.

four_box.note: tailwind yes (JJM 2.0 extended to 2028 + AMRUT/Namami Gange, plus new BESS/renewables government push -- structural, multi-year); tam yes (order book 6.4x revenue, 24-36mo visibility, large underpenetrated spend pool); moat weak (competitive-bid EPC/HAM, no pricing power despite HAM track record + early BESS-mover edge); valuation weak (P/E re-rated to 17.6x from ~12x at light-pass stage against decelerating PAT growth + WC/OCF stress).

shareholding_pattern.note: Promoter holding stable-to-rising (70.02%->70.19%) with no disclosed pledge -- not the promoter-exit pattern. But FII+DII combined fell sharply from ~6.6% to ~1.4% over the same window; institutional selling alongside rising leverage and working-capital stress is worth watching even though it doesn't trip the formal concurrent-red-flag test.

working_capital.note: Net working-capital cycle stretched from 24 days (FY24) to 137-166 days (FY26, sources vary slightly) driven by unbilled revenue (195 days) from delayed AMRUT fund releases; inventory/receivable/payable day-count breakdown not cleanly disclosed in sources reviewed. Water-EPC peers (e.g. VA Tech Wabag) typically run tighter cycles, so this reads worse than sector.

sector_kpis.note: up sharply from ~2x a year earlier (242% YoY order-book growth)
first BESS orders won Mar 2026 (NTPC, Rs1,070cr)
day-count rising is the key driver of working-capital stress; linked to AMRUT fund-release delays -- a negative trend despite the 'declining' label describing deteriorating cash conversion

scenario_analysis.note: Base case (FY26-28 revenue CAGR ~25%, margin normalizing to ~19% per FY27 guidance) lands almost exactly at CMP, consistent with gap_direction 'priced-in'. Bull needs margin to hold near FY25 levels (21%+) while renewables scales; bear assumes working-capital stress forces a growth slowdown and margin stays depressed near 16%.
